skill.name: stop-slop
skill.description: Remove predictable AI writing patterns from prose during drafting, editing, and review.
skill.summary: Clean up AI-style prose by cutting filler, formulaic structures, and predictable rhythms.

content.value_statement: AI-assisted prose can sound predictable and generic. Stop Slop helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code replace formulaic patterns with direct writing.
actual_capabilities: Identifies throat-clearing openers and filler phrases.
Suggests plain alternatives for common business jargon.
Flags formulaic structures such as binary contrasts and rhetorical setups.
Scores drafts on directness, rhythm, trust, authenticity, and density.
Provides before-and-after rewrite examples for common AI-style patterns.
limitations: Does not verify facts or sources.
Does not detect plagiarism or prove authorship.
Requires judgment for brand voice and domain terminology.
Reference lists are examples, not complete detector rules.

use_cases.title: Edit Blog Drafts
use_cases.description: Remove predictable AI phrases from articles before publication.

use_cases.title: Polish Product Copy
use_cases.description: Turn generic feature copy into shorter, clearer product language.

use_cases.title: Review Team Messages
use_cases.description: Make announcements and internal updates sound direct and human.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Cleanup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a short draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Stop Slop to revise this draft. Remove AI-style phrases, filler, and formulaic structure while keeping my meaning: [paste draft]

prompt_templates.title: Score a Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this draft with the Stop Slop scoring dimensions. Give scores, list the top issues, then provide a cleaner revision: [paste draft]

prompt_templates.title: Preserve Voice
prompt_templates.scenario: Rewrite while protecting a specific tone.
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise this text for Stop Slop patterns while preserving my tone, terminology, and audience. Explain only the highest-impact changes: [paste text]

prompt_templates.title: Compare Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Create two revised versions of this draft: one concise and one polished. In both, remove predictable AI patterns and note tradeoffs: [paste draft]

output_examples.input: Here is the thing: building products is hard. Not because technology is complex. Because people are complex.
output_examples.output: Building products is hard. Technology is manageable. People are not.

output_examples.input: In a fast-paced market, we need to lean into uncertainty and navigate challenges with clarity.
output_examples.output: We need to handle uncertainty clearly.

output_examples.input: What if the best teams do not optimize for productivity? Here is what I mean: they optimize for learning.
output_examples.output: The best teams optimize for learning, not productivity.

best_practices: Use the skill after drafting, when meaning is already clear.
Keep terms that match the audience or brand voice.
Ask for a score before requesting a full rewrite.
anti_patterns: Do not remove every phrase just because it appears in a reference list.
Do not use the skill as proof that text was written by AI.
Do not replace precise technical language with vague plain language.

faq.question: What does Stop Slop do?
faq.answer: It helps remove predictable AI-style phrases, structures, and rhythms from prose.

faq.question: Does it detect AI-written text?
faq.answer: No. It edits writing patterns but does not prove how text was created.

faq.question: Can it preserve my voice?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask it to keep your tone, audience, and required terminology.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it rewrite long documents?
faq.answer: Yes, but section-by-section review gives better control over tone and meaning.

faq.question: Is it useful for technical writing?
faq.answer: Yes, when used carefully. Keep exact terms and remove only generic filler.
